headline: UK households face energy bill rise of 443 pounds from January
pages: Gas and electricity bills for a typical UK household are forecast to rise by 443 pounds a year from January, the BBC reports. Devon Communities Together said it is hosting drop-in sessions across the county with help on energy bills, smart meters and switching suppliers. Heating oil prices have also climbed sharply this year, from about 60p to 1.11 pounds a litre, according to the Action with Communities in Rural England network. Devon County Council said many rural households rely on heating oil because they are not connected to mains gas. Charity chief executive Nora Corkery said behind every statistic is a household rationing heating or putting off filling a tank.
The sessions offer confidential one-to-one support to find financial help, and a limited number of free winter warm packs are available to those who attend. Source: BBC.
